# Synthetic validation study (generated by scripts/validation_study.py)

8 seeds x 3 cells = 24 cell experiments; forecasts at [700, 800, 900] cycles (data window 700); 95% bootstrap PIs (n=80). EOL error reported only where true EOL <= 1050 (identifiable).

| Metric | Median | Worst (max; coverage/F1: min) |
|---|---:|---:|
| q0_err | 0.0080 | 0.0435 |
| fc_rmse | 0.0105 | 0.0469 |
| coverage | 0.6667 | 0.0000 |
| width | 0.0216 | 0.0302 |
| eol_err | 0.0661 | 0.4250 |
| f1 | 0.6970 | 0.3333 |

Interpretation (read honestly): medians sit inside the benchmark task's tolerances, but worst-case seeds exceed them -- small injected outliers (down to x0.97) are partly undetectable in principle, capping F1; generator drift is not part of the scored truth model, inflating forecast error; and PI coverage at extrapolated cycles runs well below nominal 95% (residual independence assumption). The benchmark therefore uses seed-screened identifiable instances with thresholds calibrated on two independent implementations, while these random-seed numbers describe general method variability. See README.
